purpose: Triggering eval set for the ideogram skill's description. Encodes the author's rule (2026-08-26): BUILD an ideogram only on an explicit action-verb request that names it; RUN/operate an existing one is fine; a concept question or 'would one help?' may load the skill to DISCUSS/RECOMMEND but must not build; incidental mentions and requests for the deliverable itself must NOT trigger. The loop's label is the binary `should_trigger`; `category` and `rationale` are for human review and to document intent.
description_under_test: Author, run, or explain "ideograms" — living, self-contained request documents that behave like an agent brief a human (or Claude) can converse with. BUILD one only on an explicit action-verb request that names it: "make / write / create an ideogram that…", "turn this ask into an ideogram", "send X as an ideogram to Y". Also use to RUN an existing ideogram — satisfy it from the relevant files, or assess whether a draft delivery meets it ("is this sufficient to answer the ideogram?") — or on a file named `*ideogram*.md`. May also be consulted to EXPLAIN or RECOMMEND ideograms ("what is an ideogram?", "would an ideogram help capture this?"): in that case discuss and offer, do NOT start building one. Do not trigger on an incidental mention of the word alone.
notes_for_reviewer: RULED 2026-08-26 (author): 'load to recommend, not build'. The skill may fire to RECOMMEND itself when a request describes its DISTINCTIVE function (a precise ask a collaborator responds to and self-checks against) or asks whether one would help — but must not build unasked. Hence t12 and t20 are should_trigger=true, category 'discuss'.

The guarding line: t19 ('capture my insights in a document') stays a negative — generic doc creation is NOT an ideogram cue. Only the distinctive self-checkable-ask function is. This keeps the recommend-gate from waking on every document request.
The triggering loop only measures load / no-load. The build-vs-discuss behavior (once loaded) is enforced by SKILL.md §1a, not by this set.

queries.query: Make an ideogram for the Q3 status report I owe my VP.
queries.rationale: Action verb 'make' + names it.

queries.query: Write an ideogram that asks a collaborator to hand off their eval harness and make it reproducible on my machine.
queries.rationale: Action verb 'write' + names it; software-handoff shape.

queries.query: Turn this rough ask into an ideogram I can send to the whole team.
queries.rationale: Explicit 'turn this into an ideogram'.

queries.query: Send my knowledge-graph project as an ideogram to my co-founder.
queries.rationale: Package/send phrasing that names it.

queries.query: Create an ideogram to capture exactly how the churn-model experiment was set up.
queries.rationale: Action verb 'create' + names it; experiment-capture shape.

queries.query: Draft an ideogram explaining the certified-tacit-knowledge concept to a new hire.
queries.rationale: Action verb 'draft' + names it; concept-brief shape.

queries.query: Satisfy this ideogram from the files in my project directory since last month.
queries.rationale: Runs an existing ideogram.

queries.query: Is this draft sufficient to answer the Sep 9 report-out ideogram?
queries.rationale: Self-check / sufficiency read on an existing ideogram.

queries.query: Run reporting/q3_status_ideogram.md against my directory and draft my track.
queries.rationale: Names a *ideogram*.md file and asks to run it.

queries.query: Check my response against the ideogram's success criteria.
queries.rationale: Grading a draft against an existing ideogram's bar.

queries.query: What's an ideogram, exactly, and how is it different from a spec?
queries.rationale: Concept question; skill loads to explain, must NOT build.

queries.query: Would an ideogram be beneficial to capture this knowledge before our senior technician retires?
queries.rationale: BORDERLINE. Loads to recommend/offer, must NOT build. Flip to false if you want no fire on 'would it help?'.

queries.query: Write me a project status report for my VP covering Q3.
queries.rationale: Wants the report itself, not an ideogram to solicit it.

queries.query: Draft an email to a collaborator asking them to send their harness code.
queries.rationale: Wants an email; shares 'handoff' vocabulary only.

queries.query: Write a README documenting how the churn-model experiment was set up.
queries.rationale: Wants a README; capture-shaped but not an ideogram.

queries.query: Explain the certified-tacit-knowledge concept to me.
queries.rationale: Wants a concept explanation unrelated to ideograms.

queries.query: We used an ideogram last quarter and it worked great — anyway, can you pull the Q2 numbers?
queries.rationale: Incidental name-drop; the real task is pulling numbers.

queries.query: Add a section to my proposal budget narrative.
queries.rationale: Unrelated; belongs to a budget-writing skill.

queries.query: Capture my hard-won insights about the instrument in a document.
queries.rationale: Wants the capture document itself — the thing an ideogram solicits — but no request for an ideogram.

queries.query: Help me write a precise request my colleague can respond to and check their work against.
queries.rationale: RULED true (2026-08-26): describes the ideogram's DISTINCTIVE function (a self-checkable, respondable ask) without naming it — skill loads to recommend/offer, must NOT build. Contrast t19, a generic 'write a doc' ask that stays a negative.
